questions.q: In the lab scenario, what is the real table name for a table named "Visitor" inside scope `x_acme_vms`?
options: visitor
x_acme_vms.Visitor
x_acme_vms_visitor
sys_scope_visitor
questions.explain: ServiceNow prefixes the table's display name with the scope identifier to produce the real table name.

questions.q: Why does the Business Rule script on the Visit Log table not need to type the scope prefix explicitly anywhere in its code?
options: Because the scope prefix only applies to Script Includes, never to tables
Because the script was written before the application had a scope
Because Business Rules are exempt from scoping rules
Because current is already scoped to the real, prefixed table name it's running on
questions.explain: The prefix lives in the table's real name, not in every reference to current — naming isolation works quietly in the background.

questions.q: Why was it correct to leave BadgeNumberFormatter's "Accessible from" field at "This application scope only"?
options: Because Script Includes can never be set to "All application scopes"
Because there is no legitimate caller outside x_acme_vms, so widening access would be an unnecessary, unaudited grant
Because the default setting cannot be changed once an application is created
Because BadgeNumberFormatter is a table, not a Script Include
questions.explain: With no real cross-scope need, the default-closed setting is the correct, least-privilege choice.

questions.q: Why did DirectoryLookup get a targeted Cross-Scope Access Control grant instead of being opened to all application scopes?
options: Because Cross-Scope Access Control is required for every Script Include with more than one function
Because it touches real employee data, so a targeted, auditable grant to the one legitimate caller (x_acme_itsm) is the safer choice
Because x_acme_itsm is the Global scope
Because "All application scopes" cannot be used on any Script Include named DirectoryLookup
questions.explain: A targeted grant keeps DirectoryLookup closed to the rest of the instance while giving the one real caller exactly the access it needs.

questions.q: How are the Visitor and Visit Log tables, the two Script Includes, and the Cross-Scope Access Control record all grouped together in Studio?
options: They are grouped under Global scope by default
Automatically, under the x_acme_vms application record, because everything was created inside that scope's Studio context
They are grouped only if an admin creates a custom folder for them
They are not grouped together at all and must be linked manually
questions.explain: Studio's automatic, scope-tracked organization from Lesson 22 files every artifact under its owning application with no manual step.
